primitives.note: Yasuo's total critical strike chance is doubled from all other sources and his crits deal only 95% of normal crit damage; Steel Tempest and Last Breath's crit-affecting damage can crit; Steel Tempest's crit multiplier applies only to its AD-ratio term, not its flat base damage (see unsettled).
Every 1% total critical strike chance in excess of 100% converts into 0.5 bonus AD.
For 15s after Last Breath, Yasuo's critical strikes ignore 60% of the target's bonus armor (stacks additively with other percent armor pen).

Steel Tempest builds Gathering Storm (max 2 stacks, 6s each, refreshing on hit) which empowers the next Q into a whirlwind; Sweeping Blade builds Ride the Wind (max 4 stacks, 5s each) adding +25% E damage per stack, up to +100% at max stacks.

At 2 Gathering Storm stacks the next Steel Tempest cast is consumed to become an empowered whirlwind instead of a thrust; against a single target both variants deal the same base+ratio (and crit) damage.

Steel Tempest's cooldown (base 4s) and thrust cast time (base 0.35s) both shrink with Yasuo's bonus attack speed per the wiki's static/custominfo formulas; the bin only lists a flat per-rank 4s cooldown.
Base on-cast/on-impact damage instances: Q's thrust/whirlwind, E's impact damage, R's knockup-resolution damage.

Way of the Wanderer's Flow shield (125-600 by level, lasting 1s) triggers once 100 Flow stacks are reached and Yasuo takes champion/monster damage; relevant only when Yasuo is the survival-fight target, not to damage dealt.

needsBespoke.why: Two mechanics fall outside the closed primitive list's expected shape. (1) Steel Tempest's crit formula (TotalDamageCrit = BaseDamage + (ADRatio x critDamage) x ad) applies the crit multiplier only to the AD-ratio term, not to the flat base damage, unlike the usual whole-instance crit scaling a generic crit-interaction primitive would assume; combined with Yasuo's doubled crit chance, 0.95 crit-damage multiplier, and excess-crit-to-AD conversion, the layered crit math needs bespoke computation rather than a single multiplier. (2) Last Breath's cast requirement (a nearby airborne enemy champion from a genuinely 'enemy' source, excluding self/ally-applied displacement per the wiki notes) creates an open question about whether Yasuo can even cast R off his own Q-whirlwind knockup in a 1v1 dummy fight with no third-party CC; resolving whether R is castable at all, and when, needs bespoke rotation logic rather than a generic plain-cast/target-debuff treatment.

unsettled.question: Can Yasuo cast Last Breath (R) on the dummy using his own Steel Tempest whirlwind knock-up, or does R require an airborne source other than Yasuo himself, making R uncastable in a 1v1 fight with no other champion's CC?
options: Yasuo's own Q-whirlwind knockup on the enemy counts as an enemy-applied airborne source (from the target's perspective) and satisfies R's cast requirement, matching the known live-game Q3->R combo
The wiki's note that self/ally-applied displacements do not qualify excludes Yasuo's own knockup, so R cannot be cast in a pure 1v1 fight without an external CC source
quotes: ''Last Breath'' requires the target to be affected by {{tip|airborne}} from an {{tt|enemy source|from the target's perspective}}

Self-applied or allied-applied {{tip|airborne|displacements}} do not allow ''Last Breath'' to target the champion. Those applied by the ''neutral'' team (e.g. {{uis|Dragon}} initial knock back) '''can''' be targeted.

unsettled.question: Is Steel Tempest's crit-damage scaling truly limited to only the AD-ratio portion of its damage (per the bin's explicit formula), or should the whole Q damage instance (base + ratio) be scaled by the crit multiplier as the wiki's single leveling line for 'Critical Strike Damage' might suggest?
options: Only the 105% AD-ratio term is multiplied by crit damage; the flat base damage never benefits from crits, per YasuoQ1Wrapper#TotalDamageCrit = BaseDamage + (ADRatio x critDamage) x ad
The entire Q damage value (base + AD ratio) is scaled uniformly by the crit multiplier when it crits

unsettled.question: Does Sweeping Blade's per-target cooldown (6-10s by rank, starting on dash-start) gate how often E can be recast on the single dummy target, effectively overriding the much shorter 0.5-0.1s ability cooldown in this fight?
options: Yes: against a lone target E can only be recast once the per-target cooldown (6-10s) expires, so E contributes far less frequently than its raw cooldown implies
No: the per-target cooldown is a niche anti-stacking rule not meant to bind a single-target dummy simulation, so E should be modeled at its raw 0.5-0.1s cooldown

unsettled.question: Do the damage-fight and survival-fight environments let Yasuo move enough to generate Flow stacks (needed for his passive shield), or is he treated as effectively stationary like the dummy so Flow never completes?
options: Yasuo is assumed to move (attack-moving, dashing with E) enough over the ~15s window to reach 100 Flow stacks and gain the shield at least once
Yasuo, like the dummy, is treated as stationary aside from ability casts, so Flow accumulation is negligible and the shield essentially never triggers within the fight
quotes: '''Yasuo''' generates a {{tip|stack}} of {{tip|Flow}} for every {{pp|{{#var:f1}} to {{#var:f13}} for 3|1 to 13}} units he travels by any means.

proposal: Open with Steel Tempest (Q) on the dummy to start Gathering Storm stacking and apply its on-hit/on-attack effects.
Auto-attack the dummy continuously, weaving attacks between ability casts and letting Q's on-hit effects and any crit-derived bonus AD apply.
Cast Sweeping Blade (E) toward the dummy once available to deal its magic damage and build a Ride the Wind stack, respecting its per-target cooldown before recasting it on the same target.

Recast Steel Tempest (Q) every time its (attack-speed-reduced) cooldown is up; every second hit consumes 2 Gathering Storm stacks to fire the empowered whirlwind instead of the thrust, dealing the same damage against the single target.

If Last Breath (R) is castable against the dummy (pending the airborne-source ruling), cast it immediately after a Q-whirlwind knockup for its large burst damage and to open the 15s bonus-armor-penetration window on Yasuo's crits, then keep auto-attacking/critting to benefit from that debuff.
Repeat the Q-on-cooldown / auto-attack / periodic-E loop, using R again if its 30-70s cooldown (rank-dependent) comes back up within the fight window, for the remainder of the ~15s fight.
questions: Is Last Breath actually castable in this 1v1 dummy scenario given the airborne-source ambiguity, and if not, should R be dropped from the rotation entirely?

What gear/attack-speed assumption should be used to compute Steel Tempest's reduced cooldown and cast time, since these scale continuously with bonus attack speed rather than by discrete ability rank?
How should Sweeping Blade's per-target cooldown be handled against a single dummy target: is E cast once as an opener, or repeatedly at its 6-10s per-target cadence throughout the fight?

Should the rotation prioritize weaving basic attacks between every Q cast (to benefit from on-hit effects) over minimizing ability-cast downtime, or does Q's cast time make pure ability-priority higher DPS?
